data.narrative:
CreateMe is a robotics and manufacturing company at an undisclosed stage with five founders (Campbell Myers, Ben Waller, Jason Bennett, Joy Wheeler, Vibhav Prasad). The comparable universe consists of 11 same-sector peers—1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median triangulation method is not applicable to CreateMe's valuation. The analysis identified 11 robotics and manufacturing peers, but none satisfied the filtering criteria necessary for reliable median pricing. Specifically, the dataset yielded zero same-stage comparables, zero adjacent-stage comparables, and zero similar-valuation-tier comparables—falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold required for statistical confidence. A fall-back to all-sector median would introduce unacceptable distortion given the wide dispersion in stage and valuation tiers across the broader robotics sector.

Without sufficient narrow-set peer data, this analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range. The primary constraint is stage and valuation-tier clarity: CreateMe's position within the robotics funding landscape remains insufficiently resolved relative to the available peer set. Establishing valuation credibility would require either (1) stage disclosure enabling more precise peer filtering, or (2) expansion of comparable data beyond the current 11-peer universe to unlock subset-level triangulation. Key uncertainty centers on whether CreateMe's financial profile aligns with early-stage, growth-stage, or pre-exit peers.
